Radar açık olduğu için proper lookout sa: Assuming a proper lookout is kept because the radar is on
Radar alone ile başka gemi tespit edildi: A vessel which detects by radar alone the presence of another vessel shall determine if a close-quarters situation is developing and/or risk of collision exists. If so, she shall take avoiding action in ample time. The stability of target tracking, the relative/true vector selection and the effect of own-ship manoeuvres are checked.
Radar belirsizliği hız ve zaman marjıyla: Radar uncertainty is managed with speed and time margins.
Radar hedefi baş omuzlukta yakınlaşır; s: A radar target closes on the bow; an alteration to starboard creates risk with another target, while an alteration to port runs against the Rule 19 guidance and towards the shoal.
Radar hedefi, close-quarters ve kaçınıla: Radar Targets, Close Quarters and Course Changes to Avoid
Radar plot ve görsel trend doğrulanır, t: The radar plot and the visual trend are verified, the whole length of the tow is taken into account, and an early manoeuvre with a wide safety margin is prepared; until the uncertainty is resolved, speed is reduced and the master is called.
Radar plotting exercise yalnız CPA hesab: A radar plotting exercise should show not only the CPA calculation but also the effect of the chosen course/speed manoeuvre on the other targets and the direction restrictions of Rule 19(d).
Radar/AIS/ARPA bilgisini görsel ve işits: Cross-checking radar/AIS/ARPA information without letting it replace visual and aural lookout
RAM işaretini mutlak geçiş hakkı olarak: Interpreting a RAM signal as an absolute right of way
Restricted visibility checklist, ekipman: The restricted visibility checklist should cover not only the state of the equipment but also confirmation of the bridge team's division of duties and engine readiness.
Restricted visibility işaretleri ve dikk: Restricted Visibility Signals and Attracting Attention
Restricted visibility yalnız sis değildi: Restricted visibility is not only fog; it covers any condition in which visibility is restricted by mist, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, sandstorms or similar causes. Rule 19 applies to vessels not in sight of one another when navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility. Being just outside a fog bank does not take a ship out of the scope with respect to approaching targets.
Reynolds sayısı eylemsizlik kuvvetinin v: The Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces.
Rijit kaplinler (flanşlı) hiçbir kaçıklı: Rigid couplings (flanged) allow no misalignment and need perfect alignment (e.g. shaft line flanges). Flexible couplings (rubber element, gear, disc) tolerate some angular/parallel/axial misalignment, damp torsional shocks and reduce the transmission of vibration.
Risk = Olasılık × Şiddet formülüyle hesa: It is calculated with the formula Risk = Likelihood × Severity. A 5×5 matrix is widely used.
Risk of collision bütün mevcut araçlarla: Risk of collision is determined by all available means; if there is any doubt, risk is deemed to exist. A steady or barely changing compass bearing is the classic strong sign, but risk can exist even with an appreciable bearing change, especially when approaching a very large ship, a tow or a ship at close range. The visual bearing trend is complemented by radar plotting.
Rota değişikliği kadar hız azaltma ve wa: Reducing speed and taking way off are as much basic tools as altering course.
Rota işaretini (E/W, N/S) kadrana göre b: Forgetting to set the sign of the course (E/W, N/S) according to the quadrant.
Rota planında her bacak için Lm'i tek te: Calculate Lm for each leg of the passage plan separately; using a single Lm for the whole route increases the error.
Rotor, DC uyarma akımıyla manyetik alan: The rotor creates a magnetic field with DC excitation current. The diesel engine turns the rotor. The rotating magnetic field induces an EMF in the stator windings.
rp: Kompresör basınç oranı · wc: Kompres: rp: compressor pressure ratio · wc: compressor work · wt: turbine work
Rule 10 mümkün olduğunca dik heading ist: Rule 10 requires a heading as nearly as practicable at right angles, but safe navigation and the other rules still apply. Correcting only the ground track on the screen may make the ship's intention unclear to other ships.
Rule 13 overtaking, başka gemiye kıç doğ: Rule 13 overtaking starts with the definition of coming up with another vessel from a direction more than 22.5 degrees abaft her beam. If there is any doubt, she shall assume she is overtaking. The overtaking vessel keeps her responsibility until she is finally past and clear, even if the bearing later changes and it looks like a crossing.
Rule 14'te iki power-driven vessel recip: Under Rule 14, when two power-driven vessels are meeting on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses so as to involve risk, each alters course to starboard. If there is any doubt, she shall assume a head-on situation exists. Under Rule 15, in a crossing situation the power-driven vessel that has the other on her own starboard side is the give-way vessel and shall, if the circumstances admit, avoid crossing ahead of the other.
Rule 17'nin may/must aşamaları, mevcut m: The may/must stages of Rule 17, the current distance/time, the other ship's action and the last manoeuvre needed to avoid collision must be explained.
Rule 18, Rules 9, 10 ve 13 ile birlikte: Rule 18 is read together with Rules 9, 10 and 13.
Rule 18, Rules 9, 10 ve 13'te aksi gerek: Rule 18 sets the responsibilities between power-driven, sailing, fishing, NUC, RAM and CBD vessels except where Rules 9, 10 and 13 otherwise require. The overtaking rule comes before the relationship between vessel types; the not-to-impede provisions in narrow channels and TSSs also change the general scheme. A single memorised pyramid therefore does not solve every encounter.

Rule 35, restricted visibility içinde ve: Under Rule 35, in or near an area of restricted visibility a vessel gives periodic sound signals according to her status and movement. The signals for a power-driven vessel making way and for one underway but stopped and making no way are different; vessels such as NUC, RAM, CBD, sailing, fishing and towing vessels use their own patterns. There are bell/gong and additional signals for vessels at anchor and aground.
Rule 36, başka geminin dikkatini çekmek: Rule 36 allows a vessel to make light or sound signals that cannot be mistaken for any signal authorised in the rules to attract the attention of another vessel; dazzling the other ship with a high-intensity searchlight is not appropriate. Using a laser or deck lights must not endanger the lookout either.
Rule 37 ve Annex IV distress ve yardım i: Rule 37 and Annex IV list the signals that indicate distress and need of assistance. DSC distress alerts, EPIRBs, MAYDAY, rockets/flares, orange smoke and other recognised signals are used according to the situation and equipment. A false distress signal can have serious legal and operational consequences; test procedures must prevent a real alert.
Rules 20-31 ışıkların sunset-sunrise ara: Rules 20-31 require lights to be shown from sunset to sunrise and in other conditions where necessary, including restricted visibility, and prohibit other lights that could be mistaken for them. Shapes are shown by day. Deck working lights, advertising/service lights or accommodation lights must not impair the visibility/character of the COLREG lights.

Rule 34 sets out the course/engine manoeuvring signals for power-driven vessels in sight of one another, the signal of at least five short and rapid blasts for doubt/warning, and the overtaking intention/agreement signals in a narrow channel. If light signals are used, they carry the same meaning.

Ships with radar also take into account the characteristics of the radar, range scale limitations, sea/rain clutter, the detection of small targets and the number of targets.

The buoy system is interpreted according: The buoyage system is read according to the IALA scheme, and the world is divided into two main regions. Region A covers Europe, Africa, most of Asia and Australia — Türkiye is in Region A: when entering harbour, red marks are kept to port and green marks to starboard. Region B covers North and South America, Japan, Korea and the Philippines, and the lateral colours are REVERSED: when entering harbour, red is kept to starboard and green to port ('red right returning', as American seafarers memorise it). The critical point is that this is not a statement about colour but a passing instruction. Because the same colour can mean different sides in different regions, the first reflex on seeing a buoy symbol on the chart must be to ask 'which IALA region am I in?'. Although the region changes, the shape does not: the port-hand mark is cylindrical (can) in both regions and the starboard-hand mark is conical in both; when the colour cannot be read, the shape and topmark still give correct information. The chart often shows the buoy as a dot, but that dot marks the edge of a channel, the side on which to pass a danger, or confirmation of the approach line; the purpose of the symbol is therefore not just to inform but to guide action.

If crossing is necessary, it is done on a heading as nearly as practicable at right angles to the general direction of traffic flow; the aim is to reduce the time spent in the lane and any uncertainty about intention. Because of current, the ground track may differ from the heading.

The UKC decision is the sum of four components: (1) charted depth, (2) height of tide, (3) reducing factors (draught, squat, heel, wave trough, atmospheric pressure, swell), (4) safety margin (company SMS policy; typically 10% of draught or a minimum of 0.5–1.0 m). Many flag administrations and company SMSs require a minimum UKC policy. Squat — the dynamic sinkage that increases rapidly in shallow and narrow waters — is a critical danger; the Barrass formula is the estimate most widely used in practice.

Mercator projeksiyonu, küresel Dünya yüz: The Mercator projection is based on developing the spherical surface of the Earth onto a cylinder, and it is the basis of rhumb line (loxodrome) sailing. Meridians are shown as vertical lines parallel to one another, and parallels of latitude as horizontal lines. As latitude increases the distance between the parallels grows, tending to infinity towards the poles. This deliberate distortion makes a constant-course track a straight line on the chart.
Mercator seyri, Mercator projeksiyonunun: Mercator sailing is a constant-course (loxodrome) sailing method that uses the mathematical structure of the Mercator projection. It removes the error that plane sailing produces as latitude increases by expressing latitude in 'meridional parts' (MP — enlarged latitude), which are in the same units as minutes of longitude. On the Mercator projection the meridians are parallel and the intervals of latitude are stretched proportionally towards the poles; a constant course therefore becomes a straight line on the chart, and the course angle can be measured directly from it. It is the standard method for long east–west legs, in high latitudes and on ocean crossings.

Bilge tankında seviye şamandırası kontro: On an entry into the bilge tank to check the level sensor, the atmosphere was tested only at the manhole opening; the bottom and middle levels of the tank were not tested. A few minutes after entering, the first crew member suffered dizziness and loss of coordination.
Kurtarma refleksiyle ikinci personel, ta: Acting on a rescue reflex, a second crew member entered the tank without full equipment or a lifeline; the incident quickly turned into a near-miss with two casualties.
Permit to Work sürecinin prosedürel bir: The main root causes were that the Permit to Work process had become a procedural formality, that no multi-point atmosphere test was made, and that the role of the standby person was misunderstood as simply 'waiting'.
Ayrıca 'işi hızlı bitirme' baskısı neden: In addition, pressure to 'get the job done quickly' led to the ventilation time being cut short, and the toolbox talk before entry was not held in sufficient depth.
İkincil kök neden, kurtarma planının eki: A secondary root cause was that the rescue plan had not been rehearsed by the team; this is why unauthorised rescue behaviour appeared during the incident.
Kapalı alan girişinde O₂, H₂S, CO ve LEL: On entry into an enclosed space, O₂, H₂S, CO and LEL must be measured at the top, middle and bottom levels, and the results recorded on the permit form with the time in hours and minutes. Measurement is not a one-off; it must continue periodically throughout the entry.
Mekanik havalandırma yeterli süre çalışt: Mechanical ventilation must be run for a sufficient time; if the ventilation stops, the entry must be suspended automatically. A personal multi-gas detector must be kept switched on by everyone inside.
Giriş gözcüsü, iletişim hattı ve kurtarm: Entry must not start until an attendant at the entrance, a communication link and rescue equipment (SCBA, tripod, retrieval line) are ready. Rescue must be carried out only by a trained team; an unauthorised second entry is strictly forbidden.
SOLAS III/19.3.3 gereği en az iki ayda b: Under SOLAS III/19.3.3, a realistic enclosed space entry and rescue drill must be held at least every two months, and the measurement, communication and evacuation times reported.
Kapalı alan olaylarında ikinci kayıp çoğ: In enclosed space incidents the second casualty is often caused by the 'reflex to help'. The right reflex is not an unplanned entry but raising the alarm, isolating, and calling in the trained rescue team.
En güçlü önlem ekipman değil, prosedürü: The strongest safeguard is not the equipment but the behaviour of the team applying the procedure. Safety comes not from filling in the form but from putting what the form requires into practice on site.

Ballast Departure (Balast Kalkış) durumu: The Ballast Departure condition is the scenario in which the ship sails with ballast water only and no cargo. In ballast the displacement is low and the ship's windage area is large, so the wind heeling moment becomes more critical. Because KM differs at low displacements, a separate stability assessment is required for ballast conditions.

A pure great circle route is therefore rarely sailed.

Fuel consumption can change the position of the ship's centre of gravity considerably; depending on where the fuel tanks are, KG may rise or fall. The arrival condition must therefore meet the stability criteria in its own right.
Full Load Departure (Tam Yüklü Kalkış) d: The Full Load Departure condition is the scenario in which the ship leaves port at maximum cargo capacity with 100% fuel and fresh water and all stores fully loaded. It usually corresponds to the highest displacement and, because the VCG (vertical centre of gravity) potential is highest, it is a critical scenario for stability. In the full load departure condition the draft and trim must not exceed the load line limits, and all IMO stability criteria must be met.

Göksel kürede gözlemcinin bulunduğu nokt: On the celestial sphere the observer's position is taken as the centre, the point directly overhead as the zenith and the point opposite as the nadir. The intersection of the plane tangent at the observer with the sphere forms the horizon. The points where the Earth's axis of rotation meets the sphere are the celestial poles, and the intersection of the plane of the equator with the sphere is the celestial equator.
Göz yüksekliği, objenin tabanı deniz sev: The height of eye is subtracted if the base of the object is at sea level
Greenwich meridyeni sabit referans kabul: The Greenwich meridian is taken as the fixed reference. The position of a celestial body is expressed by its Greenwich Hour Angle (GHA), and its position relative to the observer's meridian by the Local Hour Angle (LHA). The angular difference between the two meridians is the longitude.
Greenwich zamanı ile yerel zaman arasınd: The difference between Greenwich time and local time changes the position of the celestial body. This difference is used both in finding longitude and as an input to the Hc and azimuth calculations. In this way the chain time difference → angular difference → change of position is clearly established.
Güneş gözlemi yapılırken sextant dik tut: When observing the Sun the sextant is held vertical. The index arm is moved until the Sun's lower limb touches the horizon. As the ship rises and falls in the swell, the moments of contact are watched several times and an average point of contact is chosen. When the measurement is complete, Hs = 46° 12.4′ is read from the sextant and the time of the observation is taken from the chronometer at the same moment. This value is not yet a position; the use of the sextant ends here. Everything done after this is the correction and interpretation of this measurement. If the sextant is not used correctly, the result will not be reliable however carefully the calculations are done.
Güneş’in deklinasyonu (δ) ve zenit uzakl: The Sun's declination (δ) and its zenith distance are interpreted together. The Sun crosses the meridian either north or south of the observer; this decides the sign rule, and the latitude is obtained directly.
Güneş’in yükselip alçaldığı yay izlenir;: The arc along which the Sun rises and falls is watched; local noon is the moment of greatest altitude. This moment is found not from the clock but as the point at which the altitude reaches its maximum. Longitude is not needed at this stage.
Günlük İzleme kapsamında, 12 veya 24 saa: In daily monitoring, all tanks are sounded at 12- or 24-hour intervals, the fuel reports are updated, the stability calculation is renewed on the loading computer and the noon report data are prepared. A daily stability update allows the ship's safety condition to be monitored continuously throughout the passage.
GZ eğrisi, geminin pozitif stabilite men: The GZ curve gives clear information about the ship's range of positive stability and its stability reserve. These two concepts express the safety margin the ship has left against capsizing, especially at large angles.
Harita düzeltmeleri, basılı bir deniz ha: Chart correction is the manual entry on a printed chart of changes in the marine environment that have occurred since the chart was published. A chart starts to become out of date the moment it is printed, because the maritime infrastructure is not fixed. Buoys are moved, the characters of lights are changed, new wrecks are found, depths are resurveyed and some areas are legally restricted or released. The chart does not reflect these changes by itself. An uncorrected chart is therefore not valid for navigation even if correct courses and calculations are laid off on it.
Harita düzeltmeleri, resmî olarak yayıml: Charts are corrected using the officially published Notices to Mariners. These notices state clearly which chart is affected, the type of change, its geographical position and how it is to be shown on the chart. Every correction is numbered and dated. For a chart to be valid, all corrections up to the latest published Notice to Mariners must have been entered on it.
Harita ölçeği, deniz haritasının neyi ay: Chart scale is the basic structure that determines what a chart shows in detail and what it deliberately leaves out. In navigation, scale is not only a mathematical ratio; it is a practical filter that decides which information is sufficient for making decisions, which is deliberately left out, and which chart is to be used at which stage. The same route looks different on charts of different scales, because a chart reinterprets reality according to its scale. Scale therefore answers the question “which decision is this chart right for?” before the question “how accurate is this chart?”.
Harita ölçeği, tek başına seyri güvenli: Chart scale alone does not make navigation safe, but choosing the wrong scale makes even correct calculations dangerous. If Mariner's Book dealt with this subject only by defining “large and small scale”, the user might try to manage a port approach with a coastal chart, or assume that a danger not shown on a small-scale chart does not exist. Scale should therefore be presented not as a definition but as a reflex that teaches which chart to make decisions with at which stage. Once this reflex is in place, the chart becomes an active navigation tool rather than a passive drawing.
Harita ölçeğinin en kritik etkisi, genel: The most critical effect of chart scale is on generalisation. Small-scale charts deliberately simplify detail so that they can show a large area. Small rocks, extensions of shoals, the limits of narrow channels or secondary aids to navigation may not be shown at all on these charts, or may be shown reduced to a symbol. This is not a deficiency of the chart but a direct result of its scale. On large-scale charts the same area is shown in a much smaller frame, so the depth contours are closer together, there are more soundings, and lines of buoys and the limits of prohibited areas become clear.

Ho ile Hc farkı doğrusal mesafeye dönüşt: The difference between Ho and Hc is converted into a linear distance. The difference found in minutes is read directly as nautical miles. At this stage there is no directional information; only “how much” the offset is has been determined.
Ho, Hc’den büyükse gözlemci varsayılan m: If Ho is greater than Hc, the observer is closer to the celestial body than the assumed position is, and the intercept is laid off towards the body. If Ho is less than Hc, the observer is farther from the body and the intercept is laid off away from it.
Horizontal Angle Fix, klasik seyrüseferd: The horizontal angle fix is a position-fixing method based on angle geometry that gives very precise results when applied correctly, and it plays an important role in terrestrial navigation where the sextant is in active use.
Inverse Problem of Mean Latitude Sailing: The inverse problem of mean latitude sailing gives the course and distance between two known positions and is one of the basic calculation methods of mean latitude sailing in the planning stage.

İlk kerteriz için BB₁ çizilir → LOP₁: BB₁ is drawn for the first bearing → LOP₁
İlk LOP, geminin seyri ve mesafesi kadar: The first LOP is transferred by the ship's course and distance run

Kaldırma kuvvetinin büyüklüğü, geminin ş: The magnitude of the buoyant force does not depend on the shape or material of the ship but only on the volume of water displaced and the density of the water. This relationship is expressed by Archimedes' principle and forms the mathematical basis of ship stability. The principle is defined as follows:
Kaldırma kuvvetinin etkidiği nokta, kald: The point at which the buoyant force acts is called the centre of buoyancy. It is the geometric centre of the underwater volume, and the buoyant force always acts vertically upwards through it. When the ship heels or trims, the shape of the underwater volume changes, so the position of the centre of buoyancy changes too. This movement is the basic mechanism of ship stability.
Kalıcı düzeltmeler, uzun süreli veya kal: Permanent corrections cover long-term or permanent changes. Adding a new buoy, changing the position or character of a light, or adding a new wreck to the chart belong to this group. These corrections are entered permanently on the chart and are not erased.
Kalite Kontrol Prosedürü olarak, hesapla: As a quality control procedure, the calculated results must be checked for logic. For example, if loading 500 tonnes gives a change in draft of only a few centimetres, is this consistent with the TPC? If GM is very different from what was expected, what is the reason? Simple logical checks like these are very effective in catching large errors.
Kargo Planlama fonksiyonu, konteyner gem: The cargo planning function covers bay plan optimisation on container ships, the hold loading plan on general cargo ships and weight distribution analysis on all ship types.

Kerterizler farklı zamanlarda ölçülür: The bearings are measured at different times
Kritik Olaylarda Acil Değerlendirme gere: Critical events call for an immediate assessment. Deteriorating weather (increasing wind force or wave height), a suspected cargo shift (a sudden change of heel, asymmetric rolling), tank leakage (an unexpected change of level, a trim anomaly) or any abnormal behaviour must trigger an immediate stability assessment.
Kuru Dökme Kargolar arasında tahıl (buğd: Dry bulk cargoes include grain (wheat, maize, barley, rice), ores (iron ore, copper concentrate, bauxite), coal, cement, sugar and salt. What these cargoes have in common is that they can shift as the ship rolls. The angle at which a bulk cargo shifts depends on its particle size, moisture content, density and stowage method.

Küresel üçgen, kenarları büyük daire yay: A spherical triangle is a figure whose sides are arcs of great circles and whose corners lie on the surface of the sphere. The basic spherical triangle used in navigation is formed by the North Pole, the departure position and the arrival position. In this triangle the sides are expressed by the co-latitudes and the difference of longitude; the angles are quantities directly related to navigation, such as the initial and final great circle courses.

Leeway, klasik seyrüseferde küçük açı gi: Although leeway may look like a small angle, it can lead to large position errors on long passages and must always be allowed for in course and position work.
LOP, objeden gemiye doğru çizilir: The LOP is drawn from the object towards the ship

Maden cevherleri taşımacılığında en cidd: The most serious risk in carrying ores is liquefaction. Granular cargoes whose moisture content is above a certain threshold can start to behave like a liquid under the ship's vibration and motion. This happens suddenly and turns the cargo into a flowing mass like a liquid cargo; a dramatic free surface effect appears and the ship can capsize within minutes. This is why the IMO introduced the Transportable Moisture Limit (TML): the moisture content of the cargo must not exceed the TML.
Mean Latitude Sailing, basitliği ve hızı: Mean latitude sailing is widely used in traditional navigation because it is simple and quick; but if it is used without knowing its latitude and distance limits, it can lead to serious position errors.

Thanks to its simplicity and speed, mean latitude sailing is one of the cornerstones of traditional navigation; but using it without knowing its limits of validity can lead to serious course errors, especially in high latitudes and over long distances.
Mean Latitude Sailing, kısa ve orta mesa: Mean latitude sailing is suitable for short and medium distances.
Mean Latitude Sailing’de boylam farkı, p: In mean latitude sailing the difference of longitude is converted into the actual distance along the parallel.
Mean Latitude Sailing’in doğrudan proble: The direct problem of mean latitude sailing, finding a new position from course and distance, is one of the basic calculations of traditional navigation and gives a practical and quick solution, especially on passages in middle latitudes.
Mercator projeksiyon, deniz haritalarınd: The Mercator projection is the mathematical projection used for nautical charts and forms the basis of navigational calculations. It is preferred at sea not for aesthetics or geographical accuracy but for navigational accuracy. The Mercator projection preserves direction and bearing relationships, so the course, bearing, distance and position work done at sea can be carried out directly and consistently on the chart.
Mercator projeksiyonda mesafe ölçümü, ya: On the Mercator projection distance is measured only on the latitude scale. The mathematical reason is that the projection deliberately stretches the scale in the direction of latitude. This stretching makes the latitude scale a reliable reference for distance.
Mercator projeksiyonda sabit bir hakiki: On the Mercator projection the track of a ship steering a constant true course is shown as a straight line on the chart. This line is called a loxodrome. This is why courses can be drawn, measured and followed directly on Mercator charts.
Mercator projeksiyonun en ayırt edici öz: The most distinctive feature of the Mercator projection is that the meridians are drawn parallel and equally spaced, while the parallels of latitude are drawn further apart as latitude increases. Near the equator the parallels are close together; towards the poles the distance between them increases. This is a deliberate distortion and the mathematical result of the projection.
Mercator projeksiyonunda enlemler arası: On the Mercator projection the spreading of the parallels of latitude is expressed by the isometric latitude. This conversion is the basic quantity of rhumb line calculations:
Mercator projeksiyonunun bu avantajı, al: This advantage of the Mercator projection is gained at the cost of distortions of area and distance that grow rapidly with latitude. Distances measured on a Mercator chart therefore do not give the true distance directly; they must be read only from the latitude scale.
Merkez açı d derece cinsinden bulunduğun: Once the central angle d has been found in degrees, its value in nautical miles can be calculated directly:
Mesafe, D.Lat ve Departure bileşenlerine: The distance is resolved into D.Lat and Departure components
Nötr denge ise geminin küçük bir yatma s: Neutral equilibrium is the special case in which the ship, after a small inclination, tends to stay in her new position. In this state there is neither a righting nor a capsizing moment. The ship stays at whatever angle she is left. It is possible in theory, but in practical ship operation it is undesirable and rarely met.

Onay ve Belgeleme aşamasında, kaptan sta: In the Approval and Documentation stage, the master reviews and approves the stability calculations. The stability calculation sheet is signed and filed. The loading plan is recorded. These documents are legally valid for PSC inspections and any casualty investigation.
Operasyonel Değerlendirme aşamasında, be: In the Operational Assessment stage, the expected weather, the length of the voyage and particular conditions on the route (narrow waters, shallow water) are taken into account. If heavy weather is expected, increasing the GM margin and minimising the free surface effect are considered.
Orta enlem seyri, düzlem seyirin geometr: Mean latitude sailing does not abandon the geometry of plane sailing completely; it only corrects the longitude component using the mean latitude. This gives a more accurate result over short and medium distances without the need for complex projections.
Orta enlem seyrinde, seyir boyunca değiş: In mean latitude sailing the latitude, which changes during the passage, is represented by a single value. This value is the arithmetic mean of the departure and arrival latitudes. When the change of longitude is calculated, the length of a minute of longitude is taken for this mean latitude.
Ortalama enlem, başlangıç ve varış enlem: The mean latitude is defined as the arithmetic mean of the departure and arrival latitudes. It represents the latitude of the ship over the passage with a single value. In the mean latitude sailing approach, east–west distances are assessed according to the length of a minute of longitude in this latitude.
Ölçülen açı, gemi mevkiinden görülür: The measured angle is seen from the ship's position

Periyodik Gereksinimler kapsamında, yükl: As periodic requirements, the loading computer is verified annually, re-approved at 5-year intervals, and after any modification of the ship (change to a hold, added superstructure, tank modification etc.) a software update and re-approval are mandatory.
Raporlama kapsamında, şirket DPA (Design: For reporting, the company DPA (Designated Person Ashore) is informed, the classification society and the flag State are notified and, if necessary, SAR (Search and Rescue) coordination is started. All actions are recorded with their times and results.
Rhumb line (loxodrom), küre üzerindeki t: A rhumb line (loxodrome) is a curve that cuts all meridians on the sphere at a constant angle and gives a constant course throughout the passage. Its appearance as a straight line on the Mercator projection makes practical navigation much easier.
Rhumb line, küre üzerinde meridyenleri s: A rhumb line is a curve that cuts the meridians on the sphere at a constant angle. Because the Mercator projection preserves angles, this curve appears on the chart exactly as a straight line. This lets the navigator draw the track of a ship steering a constant course on the chart with a ruler in one stroke.
Rota ve mesafe, bir dik seyir üçgeni olu: The course and distance form a right-angled sailing triangle
Running fix, açık denizde pratik ve işle: A running fix is practical and useful in the open sea; but if there is a change of course or speed, or if DR discipline is weak, the result is not considered reliable. The method should therefore be used, where possible, to supplement fixes from simultaneous LOPs, not to replace them.
Running fix, göksel seyirde aynı anda el: In celestial navigation a running fix is based on bringing position lines (LOPs) that cannot be obtained at the same time to a common time, allowing for the ship's movement. Observations made at different times are combined at a single time to obtain a fix. It is a practical solution when few celestial bodies are available or when the weather does not allow simultaneous observations.
Running Fix, klasik seyrüseferde tek obj: The running fix is one of the basic terrestrial fixing methods in traditional navigation; it allows a position to be found from a single object and gives high accuracy when time and the ship's movement are applied correctly.
Running Fix, klasik seyrüseferde zaman v: The running fix is one of the basic position-fixing methods in traditional navigation; it brings time and movement into the solution and is highly reliable when applied correctly.

Rüzgâr iskele tarafından geliyorsa → gem: If the wind comes from the port side → the ship drifts to starboard
Rüzgâr sancak tarafından geliyorsa → gem: If the wind comes from the starboard side → the ship drifts to port
Rüzgâr, gemiyi yanal olarak sürükler: The wind pushes the ship sideways

Serbest yüzey etkisinin en kritik sonucu: The most critical result of the free surface effect is that it reduces the ship's effective GM. This reduction makes the ship behave as though her centre of gravity had risen.

Stabilite Kaybı Belirtileri ve bunlara k: The signs of loss of stability and the immediate actions against them can be summarised as follows:
Şamandıra düzeltmeleri, seyir güvenliğin: Buoy corrections are the chart corrections that affect navigational safety most directly. If a buoy is moved, removed or re-established, the symbol on the chart is cancelled completely and the new position is entered with the correct symbol. If the light character, colour or type of the buoy has changed, all the related descriptive information is updated together with the symbol.
t₁ anına ait LOP, geminin seyir doğrultu: The LOP for time t₁ is transferred parallel to itself along the ship's track by the distance run. This does not change the direction of the LOP; it only moves its position to time t₂.
Tank Yönetimi fonksiyonu, tüm tankların: The tank management function contains the capacity tables of all tanks, the sounding/ullage conversions and the free surface moments. As the contents of the tanks are entered, the software automatically calculates the weight, VCG, LCG and FSM values.
Taşınan LOP ile ikinci LOP’un kesişimi F: The intersection of the transferred LOP and the second LOP gives the fix
Taşınan LOP, orijinal LOP’a paralel kalı: The transferred LOP stays parallel to the original LOP.
Tehlike ile gemi arasında minimum mesafe: A minimum distance is kept between the danger and the ship
Tehlikeye teğet geçer: It passes tangentially to the danger
Tehlikeyi emniyetle teğet geçen bir doğr: A line that passes the danger safely at a tangent is chosen
Transfer Operasyonları seyir sırasında s: Transfer operations affect stability directly during the passage. When transferring fuel, port–starboard symmetry must be kept, the change in GM monitored and the number of slack tanks kept to a minimum. In ballast operations, trim optimisation, GM correction and the IMO Ballast Water Management (BWM) requirements must be assessed together. Especially during ballast exchange at sea, because the sequential method empties and refills the tanks one by one, the stability must be checked for every intermediate condition.
Transit (Leading Line), klasik seyirde e: A transit (leading line) is one of the most reliable and simplest position-fixing methods in traditional navigation and is indispensable especially in areas where navigational safety is critical.
Uyarı İşaretleri aşamasında stabilite ka: In the Warning Signs stage, the signs that a loss of stability has started must be recognised. A marked lengthening of the rolling period indicates that GM has decreased. A tendency of the ship to lean to one side from upright (a loll) shows that GM is approaching zero or has become negative. A steadily increasing angle of heel, with the ship unable to return upright by herself, indicates that a critical loss of stability has begun.
Üç LOP idealde tek noktada kesişir: Ideally three LOPs cross at a single point
Üçgen hem grafik, hem sayısal çözülebili: The triangle can be solved both graphically and numerically
Vardiya Bazında İzleme kapsamında, her v: In watch-by-watch monitoring, the fuel consumption is followed every watch, changes in tank levels are checked, the ship's draft and trim are observed and her rolling characteristics are assessed. A lengthening of the rolling period is an important sign that GM is decreasing and must be investigated at once.
Varsayılan mevki (AP), DR mevkiine yakın: The assumed position (AP) is a point close to the DR position and is the reference point for which Hc and Zn are calculated. The aim is not for it to be “the right point” but to be close enough to the true position. The intercept method works on this assumption of closeness.
VGM (Verified Gross Mass) zorunluluğu, S: Under SOLAS VI/2, the VGM (Verified Gross Mass) requirement has applied since 2016. The weighed or calculated gross mass of every container must be documented before loading. Containers without VGM information must not be loaded on board. The requirement was introduced to prevent stability casualties like those caused in the past by misdeclared weights.

Yaygın Hatalar ve bunlardan kaçınma yönt: Common mistakes and ways of avoiding them are listed below:
Yeni yapılan taramalar sonucu derinlik d: When depths change as a result of new surveys, the old values are cancelled and the new ones entered on the chart. Newly found wrecks and rocks are added to the chart with the correct symbol in the correct position. If a least depth is given for a wreck, this value is shown clearly on the chart and used directly in draft calculations.
Yerel öğle anında Ho = 63° 20.0′ ölçülsü: Let Ho = 63° 20.0′ be measured at local noon.
Yön ve mesafe mutlaka doğru olmalıdır: Direction and distance must be correct
Yükleme Bilgisayarına Giriş aşamasında,: In the Loading Computer Input stage, all the data collected are entered systematically into the software. When tank data are entered, the density and temperature values are checked. The weights and positions of the cargo are specified. Separate calculations are made for both the departure and the arrival conditions, because fuel consumption during the passage can change stability considerably.
Yükleme bilgisayarının temel fonksiyonla: The basic functions of the loading computer fall under four main headings. Under stability calculation, the software calculates the draft, trim and heel, determines KG and GM, produces the GZ curve and checks all the IMO stability criteria automatically. If any criterion is not met, it gives an alarm or warning.
Yüzerlik şartını sağlayan bir gemi, kuvv: A ship that satisfies the condition of flotation is in equilibrium as far as forces are concerned; but this equilibrium alone does not explain how the ship behaves under a small external disturbance. The essence of ship stability is how the ship responds when she is displaced from her position of equilibrium. This response is described by the states of equilibrium and is studied in three basic classes: stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium.

In the fourth stage a line is drawn thro: In the fourth stage a line is drawn through the intercept point at right angles to the Zn direction. This line is the LOP. It represents every point where the ship could have been at the moment of the sight; the ship is somewhere on this line.
In the second stage a single line is dra: In the second stage a single line is drawn from the AP. This line is Zn and represents the direction in which the celestial body is seen. Zn is not a course and not the direction the ship is heading; it only carries the information “the body lies in this direction”, measured from true north.
In the third stage the difference betwee: In the third stage the difference between Ho and Hc is treated purely as a distance, taking 1′ = 1 nautical mile. This distance is laid off along the Zn line: towards the body if Ho > Hc, away from the body if Ho < Hc. There is still no LOP at this stage; only how far and in which direction the position lies from the AP is established.

Yangın alarmında kaptanın ilk kararları:: On a fire alarm, the Master's first decisions are: the location and class of the fire are established, the general alarm is sounded, the response team (usually led by the Chief Officer) is sent with equipment (SCBA, fireman's outfit, hoses), ventilation and fire dampers are controlled, and the ship is maneuvered into a position where the wind will not fan the fire (so that the fire is carried toward the stern). Boundary cooling (cooling adjacent compartments from outside with water) is the basis for preventing the fire from spreading.
Bulk gemilerinde \"alternate hold loadin: If "alternate hold loading" is to be carried out on bulk carriers, the combinations approved by the Loading Manual and the CSR (Cargo Securing Record) are strictly followed. The MOL Comfort (2013) case is the classic example of incorrect cargo distribution leading to the loss of a ship through hull fracture.
Makine dairesi bilge suyu, ancak 15 ppm: Engine room bilge water may be discharged only through a 15 ppm Oily Water Separator (OWS), monitored by an oil content meter, while the ship is en route and outside a special area. All transfers, discharges and sludge operations are recorded in ORB Part I with time, position and quantity. On tankers, cargo/ballast operations are entered in ORB Part II.
MEPC.295(71) ile güncellenen Annex V, çö: Annex V, as updated by MEPC.295(71), divides garbage into categories (plastics, food waste, ashes, operational waste, animal carcasses, fishing gear, e-waste, cargo residues). Discharge of plastics into the sea is prohibited in all circumstances. Food waste may be discharged at least 3 NM from land and outside special areas if comminuted, and beyond 12 NM if not comminuted.
Garbage Management Plan ve Garbage Recor: A Garbage Management Plan and a Garbage Record Book are carried on every ship; they are mandatory for ships of 100 GT and above and for ships carrying 15 or more persons. The Master checks that the GRB entries fully reflect every discharge, incineration and delivery (with the reception facility receipt).
Akdeniz, Baltık, Karadeniz, Kızıldeniz v: In special areas such as the Mediterranean, the Baltic, the Black Sea, the Red Sea and the Antarctic, the discharge rules are much stricter. In the Antarctic, no garbage at all may be discharged into the sea. The Master knows the status of the sea area the ship is in (special area, ECA, PSSA) and passes this on to the crew in a briefing.
MARPOL VI Reg. 14, küresel yakıt sülfür: MARPOL VI Reg. 14 reduced the global fuel sulfur limit to 0.50% from 1 January 2020, and to 0.10% in ECAs (Baltic, North Sea, North American, US Caribbean). The ship either uses compliant low-sulfur fuel (VLSFO/MGO) or achieves equivalent compliance with a scrubber (EGCS). The Master checks the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) and the retention of samples (12 months).
Lağım suyu, onaylı sewage treatment plan: Sewage may be discharged after treatment in an approved sewage treatment plant, at a certain distance from land (comminuted/disinfected ≥3 NM, treated ≥12 NM, ship proceeding at more than 4 knots). Stricter rules apply to passenger ships in special areas such as the Baltic. The Master checks that the STP is in working order and that the discharge records are kept properly.
BWM Convention, istilacı türlerin taşınm: The BWM Convention introduces the D-1 (ballast water exchange) and the final D-2 (biological treatment) standards to prevent the transfer of invasive species. Ships are fitted with IMO type-approved BWMS (UV, electrochlorination, ozone). The Ballast Water Record Book records every ballast uptake/discharge/exchange operation; the Ballast Water Management Plan is ship-specific.
Tipik bir kuru yük gemisinde taşınması g: The main certificates that must be carried on a typical dry cargo ship are: Cargo Ship Safety Construction (SafCon), Cargo Ship Safety Equipment (SafEquip), Cargo Ship Safety Radio (SafRadio), IOPP (MARPOL Annex I), IAPP (Annex VI), ISPP (Annex IV — sewage), IEEC (Energy Efficiency), ISSC (ISPS), SMC (ISM), the MLC certificate, IBWMC (Ballast Water), Tonnage, Load Line, the Minimum Safe Manning Document and the CLC/Bunker insurance certificates. Most have a validity of 5 years but are subject to annual, intermediate and renewal surveys and their windows.
Kaptanın pratik çıkarımı şudur: geminin: The practical conclusion for the Master is that the ship's past deficiencies and the company's record directly determine today's inspection frequency. A single detention can push the company into the grey/black band and increase the probability of every ship in the fleet being targeted. For this reason, the Master is not content with saying "I passed my own inspection"; the Master knows that every finding affects the company's record and the fleet risk.
Her deficiency, bir konu koduna (örn. 07: Each deficiency is linked to a subject code (e.g. 07 fire safety, 11 safety of navigation, 01 certificates, 04 emergency systems, 18 ISM) and to one or more action codes. The action code states what the inspector requires of the ship: 16 = "rectify deficiency", 17 = "rectify at next port", 18 = "rectify within 14 days", 15 = "rectify before departure" and, the most serious, 30 = "detainable deficiency / ship detained".
Kaptan, bir bulgunun action kodunu rapor: The Master must always read the action code of a finding before signing the report, because the difference between "rectify before departure" (15) and "detained" (30) is an operational and commercial chasm that keeps the ship from sailing. A code 30 is a sign not only of that finding but of a systemic doubt about the safe operation of the ship.
Kaptanın hafife almaması gereken nokta,: What the Master must not underestimate is that "the sum of several small findings" can lead to detention just as "a single major failure" can. If the inspector sees a picture of individually minor findings that together prove the SMS has collapsed, the inspector may detain the ship under ISM (code 18). In other words, the ship may be detained on the grounds that "none of them is fatal on its own, but together they show the absence of a system".
Hazırlığın en kritik ve en çok ihmal edi: The most critical and most neglected part of preparation is preparing the crew for the inspection. Every crew member must be able to demonstrate their own muster station, fire and abandon ship duties, and the use of the EEBD and immersion suit. When the inspector stops a randomly chosen crew member (oiler, AB) and asks "what do you do on a fire alarm?", a correct answer given without hesitation is the strongest evidence that the system works.
PSC raporunda kaptan, deficiency'lerin a: In the PSC report, the Master must read carefully the action codes of the deficiencies, the rectification period and the notes on the ship. In the case of a code 30 (detention), the Master immediately informs the company, the DPA, the flag State, class and the P&I/H&M side, and coordinates the survey and re-inspection process required to lift the detention. Where necessary, there is a right to a formal appeal (appeal/review) via the flag within 90 days.
ISPS Code çerçevesinde gemide Ship Secur: Under the ISPS Code there is a Ship Security Officer (SSO) on board and a Company Security Officer (CSO) ashore. The Master coordinates with the SSO and CSO on security matters; however, the ISPS Code states clearly that not even security grounds can override the Master's priority for safety and security. The Security Level (1/2/3) is set by the flag/coastal State; a change of level is passed to the ship immediately and the appropriate measures (access control, patrols, restricted areas) are stepped up.
Yüksek riskli bölgelerde (Aden Körfezi,: In high-risk areas (Gulf of Aden, Gulf of Guinea, approaches to the Singapore Strait), the Master manages, within the BMP framework (Best Management Practices, currently BMP5/MSCHOA), reporting to UKMTO, hardening measures (razor wire, citadel, water hoses), group transit/convoy and, if necessary, coordination of an armed security team (PCASP). All this coordination is planned in advance with the CSO and the company.
OCM 15 ppm'i aşarsa 3-way valve sintiney: If the OCM exceeds 15 ppm, the 3-way valve returns the bilge water to the tank; discharge is made outside special areas and at the appropriate distance. It is entered in ORB I with the correct code.
OWS çıkışı OCM ile izlenir; 15 ppm aşılı: The OWS outlet is monitored by the OCM; if 15 ppm is exceeded, the automatic 3-way valve returns the bilge water to the tank. Discharge is made outside special areas and away from the coast (at an appropriate distance).
ORB Part I (machinery space operations): ORB Part I (machinery space operations) and Part II (cargo/ballast — on tankers) are completed under MARPOL Annex I immediately after each operation, with the relevant coded item (A to K). Slop, bilge, sludge and oily water separator (15 ppm) discharges, internal transfers and waste deliveries are recorded. Each page is signed by the Master.
Garbage Record Book, MARPOL Annex V kaps: The Garbage Record Book holds the records of discharges, incineration and deliveries to port reception facilities by waste category (A-J) under MARPOL Annex V. The Ballast Water Record Book records ballast uptake/discharge, treatment and exchange operations under the BWM Convention. Both books are open to inspection, and missing entries are grounds for a finding (deficiency).

Galley/store kapı ve açıklıklarını emniy: Secures the galley/store doors and openings.
Yaşam mahallindeki su, elektrik veya kay: Reports water, electrical or slip hazards in the accommodation.
İlk yardım ve personel ihtiyaçları için: Prepares the support area for first aid and personnel needs.
Oksijen/ilk yardım donanımını eğitimli m: Prepares the oxygen/first aid equipment for trained medical personnel.
Kazazedenin ısı kaybını önleyecek kuru v: Prepares a dry, controlled area to prevent heat loss from the casualty.
Kurtarma alanına izinsiz girmez ve tıbbi: Does not enter the rescue area without permission and follows medical instructions.
Temiz su, temiz PPE ve hijyen malzemesin: Prepares clean water, clean PPE and hygiene material outside the dirty zone.
Kontamine giysi ile galley/yaşam alanı a: Prevents cross-contamination between contaminated clothing and the galley/accommodation.
Müdahale ekibinin içme suyu ve dinlenme: Meets the response team's drinking water and rest needs safely.
Yalnızca emniyetliyse atanmış kamara/ort: Checks the assigned cabin/common area sweep route only if it is safe.
Bulunan, eksik veya yardıma ihtiyaç duya: Reports persons found, missing or needing assistance to the muster officer.
Yangın kapıları ve kaçış yollarını açık/: Secures fire doors and escape routes open or closed as required.
Emniyetliyse atanmış fire door, porthole: If safe, closes the assigned fire doors, portholes and ventilation openings.
Dumanlı koridora bağımsız girmez; tamaml: Does not enter a smoke-filled corridor independently; reports the sweep areas completed.
Atanmışsa sedye ve ilk yardım ekibine ka: If assigned, joins the stretcher and first aid team.
Atanmış kamara/ortak alanın boşaltıldığı: Reports that the assigned cabins/common areas have been evacuated.
İlave can yeleği, battaniye ve ilk yardı: Brings extra lifejackets, blankets and the first aid kit to the station.
Kişi hesabı ve doğru craft'a yönlendirme: Helps with the headcount and directing people to the right craft.
Sedye, battaniye, kuru giysi ve ilk yard: Prepares the stretcher, blankets, dry clothing and first aid area.
Kazazedenin mahremiyetini ve sıcak tutul: Ensures the casualty's privacy and keeps them warm.
Tıbbi ekip talimatıyla kayıt veya ekipma: Gives record or equipment support on the medical team's instructions.
Alt seviye kamara/ortak alanları yalnızc: Checks the lower-level cabins/common areas only by a safe route.
Watertight/fire door ve açıklıkların dur: Reports the condition of watertight/fire doors and openings.
Personeli su alan veya elektrik riski bu: Moves personnel away from flooded areas or areas with an electrical hazard.
Sedye, ilk yardım ve oksijen donanımını: Prepares the stretcher, first aid and oxygen equipment for trained personnel.
Kazazedenin kabul alanını açık ve emniye: Keeps the casualty reception area clear and safe.
Kapalı mahale veya giriş kontrol sınırın: Does not pass into the enclosed space or the entry control boundary without permission.
Kirli PPE için ayrı toplama ve etiketli: Sets up separate collection for dirty PPE and a labelled temporary storage area.
Kontamine ayakkabı/giysiyle yaşam mahall: Prevents entry into the accommodation with contaminated shoes/clothing.
Temiz PPE ve hijyen malzemesi stokunu ka: Reports the stock of clean PPE and hygiene material to the person keeping the records.
Genel acil durum alarmı, PA sistemi, per: The general emergency alarm, the PA system, the crew's first actions and how the Master will give the order to abandon ship must be stated clearly.
Gerçek cetvel rütbe grubu değil, her per: The real muster list must show each crew member by name/rank with the assigned initial station, not by rank group; persons of the same rank must have separate duties.
Watertight/fire door, valf, scupper, sid: Watertight/fire doors, valves, scuppers, side openings, fans, dampers, fuel and electrical isolations must be assigned to named persons.
Her survival craft için amir, ikinci sor: For each survival craft, the commander, second-in-command, engine operator, launching crew, painter and carriers of portable communications/LSA must be designated.
Saldırı, yedek, BA control, boundary coo: Attack, back-up, BA control, boundary cooling, pump/isolation and first aid duties must be written with the team leader and the withdrawal chain.
Köprüüstü–saha–ECR haberleşmesi, kullanı: Bridge–scene–ECR communications, the equipment/channel used, the person responsible for distress communications and the incident recorder must be stated.
LSA ve FFA'nın iyi durumda ve hemen kull: The officer or officers responsible for keeping the LSA and FFA in good condition and ready for immediate use must be clearly assigned.
Kaptan, saha komutanı, Baş Mühendis, GMD: Named substitutes must be designated for the Master, on-scene commander, Chief Engineer, GMDSS operator, craft commanders and other critical duties in case personnel are unavailable or injured.
Cetvel gemi denize çıkmadan hazırlanmalı: The muster list must be prepared before the ship proceeds to sea and revised when the crew changes; it must be posted in conspicuous places on the bridge, in the engine room and in the accommodation.
Operasyonu yöneten güverte zabiti; başüs: The deck officer in charge of the operation; forward/aft team leader and authorised operator
Gemiye özgü kullanım kitabını, risk değe: Verify the ship-specific operating manual, the risk assessment, the allocation of duties and the means of uninterrupted communication.
Enerji kaynağı, lokal/acil durdurma, fre: Carry out no-load checks of the power source, local/emergency stops, brake, guards, limits and leaks; clear the fall, crushing and rope/chain recoil areas.
Uygunsa kaldırma donanımı sicili, SWL ve: Where applicable, the register of lifting appliances, SWL and certificates

Gemiye özel limit, komuta zinciri ve emn: Ship-specific limits, chain of command and safe stopping method
Köprüüstü vardiya zabiti; kritik ayar ve: The officer of the watch on the bridge; bridge team management with the Master for critical settings and deviations
Cihazın güç, self-test/BITE, sensör kayn: At the watch handover, verify the equipment's power, self-test/BITE, sensor source, date/time, dimmer and alarm status.
Ayarları seyir safhası, draft/UKC politi: Make the settings according to the phase of the voyage, the draft/UKC policy, visibility, traffic, chart coverage and the Master's night orders; do not take over the previous watch's settings blindly.
Arıza/servis kaydı; olaya ilişkin veriys: Defect/service record; VDR save if the data relate to an incident
Seyir cihazlarının gemi tipi/tonaj/yapım: Carriage of navigational equipment according to ship type/tonnage/date of build, and up-to-date official charts/publications
Emniyetli seyir vardiyası, gözcülük ve m: Safe navigational watch, lookout and the proper use of all available means
Cihaz tipine özgü fonksiyon, alarm, test: Equipment-specific functions, alarms, tests and back-up arrangements
Başmühendis gözetimindeki vardiya mühend: The engineer of the watch under the Chief Engineer's supervision; engine control confirmed with the bridge
Yağlama, soğutma, yakıt/hava, elektrik v: Before starting, verify the lubrication, cooling, fuel/air, electrical and control air auxiliaries, and the interlock, alarm and trip conditions.
Turning gear, çalışma izni/LOTO, persone: Check the turning gear, permit to work/LOTO, personnel and tools, and bridge–engine room communications; allow remote control only when local preparation is complete.
Makine jurnali ve performans trendleri: Engine room log and performance trends
Yakıt-yağ analizi ve klas/servis raporla: Fuel/lube oil analyses and class/service reports
Makine, elektrik, dümen ve acil durum dü: Machinery, electrical, steering and emergency arrangements
Emniyetli işletme, kritik ekipman, bakım: Safe operation, critical equipment, maintenance and management of non-conformities
Gemi ve makine tipine özgü limit, tolera: Limits, tolerances and tests specific to the ship and machinery type
Vardiya mühendisi veya atanmış makine za: The engineer of the watch or an assigned engineer officer; the ETO/authorised personnel for electrical work
Hat dizilimini P&ID üzerinden doğrula; t: Verify the line arrangement from the P&ID; check the tank level, suction/discharge valves, vents, drains, lubrication, cooling and electrical supply.
Stand-by ünitenin gerçekten hazır olduğu: Confirm that the standby unit is really ready, that alarms/trips are normal and that maintenance isolations have been removed.
Kimyasal/atık/servis kaydı (sisteme uygu: Chemical/waste/service record (if applicable to the system)
Temel makine, elektrik, kazan, basınçlı: Basic provisions on machinery, electrical installations, boilers, pressure systems and fire safety
Atık veya deşarj üreten yardımcı sisteml: For auxiliary systems that produce waste or discharges, the relevant Annex and approved arrangement
Hat dizilimi, interlock, normal değer ve: Line arrangement, interlocks, normal values and safe maintenance
Kaptan komutasındaki acil durum organiza: The emergency organisation under the Master's command; depending on the system, the Chief Engineer, officers and the trained fire team
Fire Control Plan, muster list, sabit si: Verify the Fire Control Plan, muster list, fixed-system release procedure, evacuation of the space and communications for the specific ship.
Valf/izolasyon konumu, güç kaynağı, alar: Visually check the valve/isolation positions, power supply, alarms, cylinder/tank pressure or pump readiness and the access seals, without changing anything.
Yetkili servis, dolum, hidrostatik test: Authorised service, refilling, hydrostatic test or inspection report
Yangının önlenmesi, algılanması, sınırla: Prevention, detection, containment and extinction of fire
Sabit ve seyyar yangın sistemlerinin tek: Technical arrangement of fixed and portable fire-fighting systems
Gemiye özgü mahal, vana, uzaktan kapatma: Ship-specific spaces, valves, remote shut-offs and release sequence
Kaptan gözetiminde birinci zabit/cargo o: The Chief Officer/cargo officer under the Master's supervision; coordination with the terminal and the engine control room
Onaylı cargo/operations manual, loading: Verify the approved cargo/operations manual, loading plan, ship/shore checklist, communications and emergency stop method together.
Hat, tank/ambar, valf, vent, seviye-bası: Before the operation, confirm the lines, tanks/holds, valves, vents, level/pressure alarms, closing arrangements and appropriate gas measurements.
CSM, test sertifikası, PMS ve defect rep: CSM, test certificates, PMS and defect report
Yük bilgisi, istifleme, sabitleme ve teh: Provisions on cargo information, stowage, securing and dangerous goods
Gemi ve yük tipine uygulanabilen çevre v: Environmental and cargo codes applicable to the ship and cargo type
Gemiye özgü hat, limit, ESD ve operasyon: Ship-specific lines, limits, ESD and operating sequence
Başmühendis/atanmış mühendis; kayıt ve d: The Chief Engineer/assigned engineer; MARPOL/BWM responsibility together with the Master for records and discharge decisions
Onaylı plan/operating manual, sertifika,: Verify the approved plan/operating manual, certificate, calibration, sampling point and line arrangement on the actual pipework.
Bypass veya mühürlü vana durumunu, sensö: Check the status of any bypass or sealed valves, the sensor/alarm self-test and the tank capacity; do not start the operation simply because a type approval exists.
İlgili resmî record book ve elektronik k: The relevant official record book and electronic record
PMS, tank sounding ve reception facility: PMS, tank soundings and reception facility documents
Sistemin ürettiği deşarj, atık veya emis: Provisions applicable to the discharges, waste or emissions produced by the system
Balast yönetim planı, D-2 standardı ve k: Ballast water management plan, D-2 standard and records
Type-approved sistemin gemiye özgü çalış: The ship-specific operating envelope and limitations of the type-approved system
Kaptan gözetimindeki GOC/ROC yetkili tel: The GOC/ROC-qualified radio officer or assigned LSA officer under the Master's supervision; muster list duties for life-saving
Gemi sertifikası, sea area, ekipman kiml: Check the ship's certificate, sea area, equipment identity/MMSI, reserve power, self-test and date/time/position input.
LSA için erişim, securing, release/HRU,: For LSA, verify access, securing, release/HRU, weekly/monthly checks and authorised service dates against the maker's instructions; do not improvise a dangerous release test.
Radio log veya GMDSS test kaydı: Radio log or GMDSS test record
LSA haftalık/aylık kontrol ve drill kayd: LSA weekly/monthly check and drill record
Can kurtarma araçları, hazır bulundurma,: Life-saving appliances, readiness, maintenance and drills
Modernize GMDSS fonksiyonları, deniz ala: Modernised GMDSS functions, sea areas and radio equipment
Filika/rescue boat, launching appliance: Authority for the maintenance/testing of lifeboats/rescue boats, launching appliances and release gear
Windlass statik demirleme yükünü tek baş: The windlass is not left to carry the static anchoring load alone; the functions of the brake, clutch and chain stopper do not replace one another.
Zincirin yönü, şakül/marka, hız, yük ve: Monitor the lead of the chain, the vertical/marks, speed, load and the angle at which it leaves the seabed together.
Fren sıcaklığı, hidrolik basınç/kaçak, m: Assess the brake temperature, hydraulic pressure/leaks, motor current and abnormal noise/vibration as trends.
Köprü ile her komutta kapalı çevrim repe: Use closed-loop repeat-back with the bridge for every order; compare the observed chain movement with the control indicator.
Demir yerine oturduğunda yükün stopper'a: When the anchor is housed, verify physically that the load has been transferred to the stopper; do not rely on the brake lever position alone.
Kontrolsüz zincir kaçırma, fren tutmamas: Do not continue the operation if the chain runs out uncontrolled, the brake does not hold or personnel enter the line of the chain.
Basınç/akım ani yükselmesi, zincirin haw: Stop and call the Master in the event of a sudden rise in pressure/current, the chain seating wrongly in the hawse pipe, or loss of communication.
Gerçek bir demir ırgadı örneği. Wildcat,: An example of a real anchor windlass. The wildcat, clutch, band brake and chain stopper arrangement varies from ship to ship; a photograph on its own is not an operating diagram.
SWL tek bir evrensel kapasite değildir;: SWL is not a single universal capacity; the outreach, jib angle, grab/spreader weight, dynamic load, trim/list and wind change the load chart.
Load chart, outreach, kanca yüksekliği,: Monitor the load chart, outreach, hook height, rope spooling, brake and limit indicators together with the movement of the load.
Rüzgâr, gemi hareketi, side-pull, yük sa: Continuously reassess the wind, ship movement, side pull, swing of the load and quality of communication.
Yük ağırlığı ve loose gear toplamını bel: Verify the total of the load weight and loose gear from documents/labels; do not lift an unknown load by guesswork.
Yüksüz fonksiyon-fren-limit testi ile fi: Check with a no-load function, brake and limit test that the physical movement matches the direction of the control.
Overload/limit alarmı, fren kaydırması,: Make the load safe in case of an overload/limit alarm, brake slip, wire damage, personnel under the load or loss of communication.
Beklenmeyen list/trim, çatlak/deformasyo: If there is an unexpected list/trim, cracking/deformation, a hydraulic leak or abnormal noise, do not continue without an authorised inspection.
Gemi güverte vinci örneği. Doğru kapasit: An example of a ship's deck crane. The correct capacity is determined not from a photograph but from that crane's load chart, SWL marking and certified loose gear records.
Auto-tension her rıhtım operasyonunda gü: Auto-tension is not a safe default in every berth operation; if the ship/terminal procedure and line arrangement are not suitable, it can cause lines to slacken and tighten in turn.
Halat lead'i, katmanlanma, aşınma, eşit: Physically monitor the line lead, layering, wear, equal load sharing and the snap-back direction.
Fren tutma, render/tension göstergesi, g: Assess the brake holding, render/tension indicator, tide/draft changes and the effect of wind/current together.
Mooring planındaki hat fonksiyonunu ve d: Verify on deck the function of the line in the mooring plan and the correct use of fairleads/bollards.
Fren test sonucu ile üretici/design MBL: Compare the brake test result with the setting based on the manufacturer's/design MBL; do not tighten by feel alone.
Personel bight/snap-back alanındaysa, ha: Stop the winch if personnel are in the bight/snap-back area, the line is jumping or communication is lost.
Fren kayması, pedestal/fairlead deformas: In the event of brake slip, pedestal/fairlead deformation or serious damage to the line, transfer the load to another line under control and report it.
Bir mooring winch kurulum örneği. Tambur: An example of a mooring winch installation. The drum, split drum, warping head and brake arrangement vary from ship to ship; the safe area is not just a painted stripe.
Cleat'leri aşırı sıkmak hasarlı conta, c: Over-tightening the cleats does not make up for a damaged gasket, compression bar or drain; a hose/ultrasonic test result is meaningful only with the correct procedure.
Panel hizası, teker/ray, hidrolik kaçak,: Monitor panel alignment, wheels/rails, hydraulic leaks, cross joints, gasket compression and the drain channel.
Kapatmada cleat yükünü dengeli uygula; c: When closing, apply the cleat load evenly; check the integrity of the coaming, drain non-return valves and access hatches together.
Kapanma sonrası fiziksel kilit/cleat poz: After closing, verify the physical lock/cleat positions and that the drains are clear by walking round with two people.
Yük/hava riskine göre yetkin kişiyle ult: Depending on the cargo/weather risk, carry out an ultrasonic or approved hose test with a competent person; do not mistake a chalk test for a watertightness test.
Panel hareket alanında kişi/engel, hizas: Stop the movement if there are people/obstructions in the path of the panels, panels out of alignment or a safety interlock fault.
Çatlak, kalıcı deformasyon, conta hattın: In the event of cracking, permanent deformation, a serious leak along the gasket line or a locking failure, escalate the decision to sail to the Master/class process.
Gerçek bir ambar kapağı örneği. Fotoğraf: An example of a real hatch cover. The photograph gives the general appearance of the type; weathertightness depends on the gasket, compression bar, cross joints and drains working together.
Capstan halatı kilitleyen bir depolama t: A capstan is not a storage drum that locks the rope; as the number of turns increases, the holding force and the risk of jamming/override increase together.
Halatın düzgün turunu, kuyruk tarafındak: Monitor the even turns of the rope, the stance of the person on the tail and the start of any override.
Motor yükü, warping head yüzeyi, ayak ku: Continuously check the motor load, the warping head surface, the return of the foot control and communications.
Halat lead'inin capstan eksenine uygun v: Before the operation, verify that the rope lead suits the capstan axis and that the fairlead is clear.
Kumandayı bıraktığında hareketin kesildi: Test at no load that the movement stops when the control is released; do not count switching the main switch as a test.
Halat üst üste binmeye, kişinin eli/giys: Stop immediately if the rope starts to override, a person's hand/clothing comes close or control of the tail is lost.
Kumanda takılması, frenlememe, anormal s: If the control sticks, it does not brake, it overheats or the pedestal is cracked, apply LOTO and report it.
Dikey capstan/warping head örneği. Halat: An example of a vertical capstan/warping head. The direction of the turns and the safe position of the operator are set by the ship's actual fairlead arrangement.
Radar her hedefi garanti ederek gösterme: Radar does not guarantee to show every target; clutter settings can remove a target, and the ARPA CPA/TCPA is an estimate that depends on the sensors, tracking time and target manoeuvres.
Brilliance, range, orientation/motion, g: Set the brilliance, range, orientation/motion, gain, tuning, sea/rain clutter and pulse to suit the conditions; check on different ranges that the automatic settings are not suppressing small targets.
Relative/true vector, vector time, targe: Do not treat CPA/TCPA as a decision value without reading the relative/true vector, vector time, target history, acquisition status and the heading/speed sensor.
Hedefi görsel kerteriz, ikinci radar, AI: Cross-check the target with a visual bearing, a second radar, the AIS identity and, if possible, the chart/PI; do not mistake an AIS symbol for a radar echo.
EBL/VRM ve paralel index'i sabit harita: Check the EBL/VRM and parallel index against a fixed charted object; if the heading marker/antenna alignment or range/bearing accuracy is in doubt, carry out a performance test.
Heading veya speed input kaybı, yanlış m: If the heading or speed input is lost, the motion/vector mode is wrong, there is a radar/antenna fault or obvious misalignment, do not trust the ARPA result and call the Master.
Kötü görüşte hedef algısı yetersizse saf: If target detection is inadequate in poor visibility, reassess the safe speed, reinforce the lookout and organise the team for early and substantial action in accordance with COLREG.
Radar performance/PM ve compass bearing: Radar performance/PM and compass bearing check record
Passage plan üzerindeki PI/clearing rang: PI/clearing range information on the passage plan
Gemi radarlarının revize performans stan: Revised performance standards for shipborne radar
Gözcülük, emniyetli hız, çatışma riski,: Look-out, safe speed, risk of collision, action to avoid collision and restricted visibility
Radar/ARPA kullanımı ve emniyetli köprüü: Use of radar/ARPA and a safe bridge watch
X-band bir radar PPI/ARPA konsolu örneği: An example of an X-band radar PPI/ARPA console. The green echoes on the screen show the real surroundings; the manufacturer's interface may be old, but the logic of range, gain, clutter, EBL/VRM, vectors and trails is the same on current radars.
ECDIS kendi başına emniyetli rota üretme: ECDIS does not produce a safe route on its own; legal equivalence depends on type approval, official and up-to-date data, correct use and an adequate independent back-up arrangement together.
Appraisal'da tüm rota için resmî ENC kap: In the appraisal, check official ENC coverage, usage band/scale, permits and update status for the whole route; in planning, check the safety depth/contour, XTD, look-ahead, no-go areas, wheel-over and abort points.
Monitoring sırasında seçili position/hea: During monitoring, watch the selected position/heading/speed source, chart scale/overscale, off-track, safety contour and special-condition alerts; do not acknowledge an alarm without understanding its cause.
Primary GNSS mevkiini radar/visual fix,: Cross-check the primary GNSS position with a radar/visual fix, a second independent PNT source or another suitable method; do not treat the radar overlay alignment as independent evidence of position.
Automatic route check sonrasında rotayı: After the automatic route check, inspect the route leg by leg visually at the largest suitable ENC scale; take mariner action for isolated dangers, CATZOC/quality, SCAMIN and temporary/preliminary information.
Resmî kapsam/permit/update yokluğu, upda: Do not approve the plan if official coverage/permits/updates are missing, an update is rejected, the datum/PNT is in doubt or the back-up arrangement cannot be used; escalate to the Master and the company procedure.
Position jump/freeze, heading uyuşmazlığ: In the event of a position jump/freeze, heading mismatch, safety alarm or unplanned deviation, first bring the ship into a safe navigational condition; do not let following the route line on the screen become an automatic reflex.
ENC update report, permit ve update reje: ENC update report, permit and update rejection record
Master-approved passage plan/revision ve: Master-approved passage plan/revision and alarm/position cross-check records
