Mediterranean MoU, Akdeniz'e kıyısı olan: The Mediterranean MoU coordinates port State control in the countries with a Mediterranean coast; its members include North African countries (Algeria, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia), Eastern Mediterranean countries (Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye), Malta and Cyprus. Because Malta and Cyprus, as EU members, also belong to the Paris MoU, the MoU works closely in line with Paris standards and shares data through THETIS-Med. This dual membership helps keep a consistent standard in Mediterranean inspections.
Akdeniz limanlarına girecek gemiler, gem: Ships entering Mediterranean ports face targeting based on ship age, type and flag performance; deficiency classification and detention conditions are in line with the IMO PSC procedures. A critical development specific to the region is the designation of the Mediterranean as a SOx Emission Control Area (ECA): since 1 May 2025 the fuel sulphur limit in the Mediterranean has been 0.10%, so ships must already have achieved fuel and scrubber compliance. Because North African ports may have additional local requirements, ships should check these before entry and review with the crew the CIC subjects coordinated with the Paris MoU.
Akdeniz'i ilgilendiren en önemli düzenle: The most important regulatory development affecting the Mediterranean is the designation of the region as a SOx Emission Control Area (ECA): under this rule, which has applied since 1 May 2025, the fuel sulphur limit in the Mediterranean has fallen from the global 0.50% to 0.10%. This requires ships either to use very low sulphur fuel or to operate an approved scrubber, and it directly affects route planning: on entering the Mediterranean the fuel changeover procedure is followed and recorded in the logbook prescribed by the flag State. Mediterranean MoU inspections are expected to focus more and more in the coming years on this new sulphur regime and on compliance with air emission rules in general. Ships entering the region should plan their fuel supply strategy and scrubber compliance for this regime.
Kuzey Afrika–Doğu Akdeniz çeşitliliği ve: North African–Eastern Mediterranean diversity and THETIS-Med
Mediterranean MoU, idari kapasite ve düz: The Mediterranean MoU has a diverse membership in terms of administrative capacity and regulatory approach: North African countries (Algeria, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia) and Eastern Mediterranean countries (Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye) sit alongside Malta and Cyprus, which are EU members. Because Malta and Cyprus are also members of the Paris MoU, the MoU works in line with Paris standards and data systems; inspection data are shared through the regional THETIS-Med platform and integrated with IMO's GISIS. Because of this diversity, ships entering the region should check in advance not only the common MoU standards but also any additional local requirements, especially in North African ports. CIC campaigns coordinated with the Paris MoU allow ships to comply with both regimes with a single preparation.
THETIS-Med ve GISIS entegrasyonunun birl: How THETIS-Med and GISIS integration work together
Akdeniz'de hem Mediterranean MoU hem de: For a ship trading in the waters of both the Mediterranean MoU and the Paris MoU, the integration of THETIS-Med and GISIS brings a concrete practical benefit. THETIS-Med collects the inspection results, deficiencies and detention records from the ports of Mediterranean MoU members at regional level; GISIS, as IMO's global data platform, carries this information into a wider international framework and forms an indirect bridge with the systems of other MoUs (including the Paris MoU's THETIS). Thanks to this integration, if for example a ship is first inspected in a Paris MoU port and a deficiency is recorded, that information becomes accessible in principle through GISIS, and when the ship later calls at a Mediterranean MoU port (for example in Morocco or Egypt) the inspector is not unaware of that history. Although in practice the data transfer is not always immediate, the two systems working together mean that a single ship's history can be followed largely consistently despite the fragmented administrative structure of the Mediterranean (EU members alongside non-EU coastal States).
1992'de kurulan Viña del Mar Agreement,: Established in 1992, the Viña del Mar Agreement is Latin America's first regional PSC agreement. With 16 member States, it coordinates inspections in the ports of South and Central America. The agreement was inspired by the Paris MoU model. Inspection capacity and standardisation in the region are supported by IMO technical assistance programmes.

Viña del Mar Agreement (Acuerdo Latinoam: The Viña del Mar Agreement (Acuerdo Latinoamericano) is Latin America's first regional port State control agreement and, with 16 member States, coordinates inspections in South America, Central America and the Caribbean. It was set up on the model of the Paris MoU and shares inspection data through the regional CIALA information system. The region has a dynamic of its own: Panama, which has one of the largest ship registers in the world, lies in this area, so the roles of port State and flag State interact intensely in the region.
Viña del Mar Agreement bölgesinin kendin: A dynamic peculiar to the Viña del Mar region is that Panama, which has one of the largest ship registers in the world, lies within it. This means the roles of flag State and port State are closely intertwined in the region: a large share of the ships passing through are Panama-flagged, so they are subject both to their own flag State's obligations and to the PSC inspections of the ports they call at. For Panama-flagged ships, making sure that their own flag State's inspection and certification processes match port State expectations is particularly important. In this context, regional PSC is not just about inspecting foreign flags; it is directly linked to the quality of one of the world's most widely used flag registers.
Latin Amerika'nın ilk PSC anlaşması olan: Latin America's first PSC agreement, Viña del Mar was set up on the model of the Paris MoU and, with 16 member States, coordinates inspections in South America, Central America and the Caribbean. Inspection data are shared through CIALA (the information centre of the Acuerdo Latinoamericano), and detention records can be seen by all members. The region's priority is to strengthen inspection capacity and standardisation among the member States; to this end it draws on IMO technical assistance programmes and develops training for inspectors and common procedures. Risk-based targeting, deficiency classification and detention criteria are in line with the IMO PSC procedures, and CIC campaigns are run in coordination with the other MoUs. Ships entering the region should check local regulations, follow CIALA inspection trends and prepare for the CIC subjects.
Viña del Mar bölgesini diğer MoU'lardan: The most striking feature that sets the Viña del Mar region apart from the other MoUs is that Panama, which has one of the largest ship registers in the world, is both a flag State and a port State lying geographically inside this MoU's area of operation. With most large open registers (such as Panama, the Marshall Islands and Liberia), the flag State function is geographically separate from the region where the ship actually trades; but in Panama's case that separation disappears. A Panama-flagged ship that transits the Panama Canal and calls at ports in the region is under two different inspection lenses at the same time: its own flag's responsibility for certification and inspection, and PSC inspection by a Viña del Mar port State — while in Panama's own ports, ships flying its flag come under flag State inspection rather than PSC. This dual position gives Panama an extra incentive to protect the quality of its register, because the detention of one of its ships in the region's ports directly affects the register's international reputation. For the other member States in the region, the heavy traffic of Panama-flagged ships brings both familiarity and the need to follow them carefully.
Viña del Mar Agreement'in 16 üye devleti: The 16 member States of the Viña del Mar Agreement cover a wide range of inspection capacity and resources: from large and relatively advanced maritime administrations such as Brazil and Mexico to small Caribbean and Central American States with more limited financial and human resources. These differences can lead to inequalities in the training of inspectors, in access to inspection equipment and even in how consistently risk profiles are calculated. CIALA tries to close this gap in two ways: first, by giving all members access to the same inspection data and deficiency codes through the regional information system, creating a minimum common language; second, through IMO technical cooperation programmes, more experienced member administrations provide instructors for inspectors and common checklists. This effort is neither linear nor quick – the differences in capacity have not been fully closed – but over time it aims to bring the quality of inspection in the region onto a more consistent line, so that which member's port a ship calls at should not greatly change how thorough an inspection it faces.

Carnot çevrimi, iki sabit sıcaklık (TH v: The Carnot cycle is the ideal reversible cycle that gives the theoretical upper limit of efficiency for all heat engines working between two fixed temperatures (TH and TC). It consists of four processes: (1) isothermal expansion (heat QH taken in at TH), (2) adiabatic expansion (TH→TC), (3) isothermal compression (heat QC rejected at TC), (4) adiabatic compression (TC→TH). In practice no real engine reaches the Carnot efficiency, but it is a reference point for assessing the thermal efficiency of real engines.

Modern large marine diesel engines operate close to this ideal cycle; the efficiency is determined by the compression ratio (r) and the cut-off ratio (rc).

Atma halatının ucuna atılan top şeklinde: A ball-shaped knot tied in the end of a heaving line. It gives the line weight so that it can be thrown further and more accurately to the quay or to another ship.
Halatı parmaklarınızın etrafına üç tur s: Wrap the line three times round your fingers.
Çımayla bu turların etrafına, onlara dik: With the working end, make three more turns round these turns, at right angles to them.
Çımayı birinci turların içinden ve ikinc: Make three more turns, passing the working end inside the first set and round the second set.
Boşluğu sarımlar boyunca sırayla alarak: Work the slack out through the turns one by one until the knot forms a ball, then secure the working end to the standing part.
İçine metal veya ağır bir cisim koymayın: Do not put metal or any heavy object inside: the heaving line may strike the people receiving it, and a heavy monkey's fist can cause serious injury.
İki halatı uç uca kalıcı olarak ekler. B: Joins two ropes end to end permanently. It is the fisherman's knot tied with double knots; it is more secure in thin and slippery line, but is hard to untie once it has been loaded.
Birinci halatın çımasını her iki halatın: Wrap the working end of the first rope twice round both ropes, back towards its own standing part, then pass it through these turns and tighten.
İkinci halatın çımasıyla aynı işlemi ter: Repeat the same with the working end of the second rope, in the opposite direction.
Doğru atılmış bağda bir yüzde iki çarpı: When tied correctly, one side shows two crosses (X) and the other side four parallel turns. Do not cut the working ends short.
Gözcükle kasa oluştur: Make a loop with the bight
Halatı ikiye katlayıp bir gözcük alın; b: Double the rope to form a bight and make a small loop with the doubled rope.
Gözcüğü kasadan geçir: Pass the bight through the loop
Gözcüğün ucunu kasanın içinden aşağıdan: Pass the end of the bight up through the loop from underneath.
Gözcüğü düğümün etrafından geçir: Take the bight round the knot
Gözcüğün ucunu açın, iki büyük kasanın e: Open out the end of the bight, pass it down round the two large loops and bring it up behind the standing parts.
Bedenleri çekerek gözcüğü düğümün üzerin: Pull on the standing parts to settle the bight on the knot; two fixed loops are formed.
Halatın uçlarına gerek kalmadan, ortasın: Forms two fixed loops in the middle of a rope without using its ends. The loops do not slip under load; it is used to spread a load between two points or, in an emergency, to lift a person.
Düğümü sıkmadan önce iki kasanın boyunu: Adjust the size of the two loops before tightening the knot. Useful when a fixed loop is needed quickly in a long rope whose ends cannot be reached.
Çımayı beden halatının etrafından geçire: Take the working end round the standing part to form a large loop.
Çımaya yakın kısımda, izbarçoda olduğu g: Make a small loop near the working end, as for a bowline.
Çımayı küçük kasadan yukarı geçirin, ark: Pass the working end up through the small loop, round behind and back down through the same loop.
İzbarçoyu sıkın; beden çekildikçe büyük: Tighten the bowline; the large loop closes as the standing part is pulled.
Halatın ucunda, beden çekildikçe daralan: Forms a running loop in the end of a rope that closes as the standing part is pulled. Used to catch and recover an object out of reach, such as something that has fallen overboard.
Kayar kasa yük altında daraldığı için as: Because the running loop closes under load, never put it round a person; for rescue use the bowline, which gives a fixed loop.
Gözcük al ve geri katla: Form a bight and fold it back
Halatta uzun bir gözcük alın ve gözcüğün: Form a long bight and fold its end back over the standing parts to make two ears.
Her kulağı yarım tur çevirerek iki küçük: Give each ear a half twist to form two small loops.
Kasaları iç içe geçir: Pass one loop through the other
Pass the left loop through the right loop.
Büyük kasaları çekip sıkın: Draw up the large loops and tighten
Her küçük kasanın içinden, alttaki büyük: Reach through each small loop and draw up the opposite side of the large bight below; when the two large loops are formed, tighten the knot.
Halatın ortasında iki sabit kasa oluştur: Forms two fixed loops in the middle of a rope. It is used to hoist a ladder or, in an emergency, a person, and to spread a load between two points.
Sıkmadan önce iki kasanın boyunu eşitley: Equalise the two loops before tightening so that the load hangs level.
Çımadan yeterli boy bırakarak halata gev: Leaving a long working end, tie a loose figure-of-eight knot in the rope.
Çımayı ringin veya bağlanacak nesnenin i: Pass the working end through the ring or the object to be secured.
Çımayı ilk sekizlinin yolunu ters yönde: Lead the working end back, following the path of the first figure-of-eight exactly in reverse.
Dört kolu ayrı ayrı çekerek çift halat k: Pull each of the four parts in turn so that the paired parts lie neatly side by side.
Halatın ucunda sabit ve çok emniyetli bi: Forms a very secure fixed loop in the end of a rope. Because it is tied by following through, the loop can be made through a ring or a harness. It jams under load and is hard to untie.
Düğümden sonra çımada halat çapının birk: Leave a tail several rope diameters long beyond the knot.
Kolları beş-altı büküm boyunca açın ve h: Unlay the strands for five or six turns of the lay and tape the end of each strand.
Gözü oluştur, ilk kolu sok: Form the eye and make the first tuck
Halatı istenen göz boyunda bükün; ortada: Bend the rope to the size of eye required and tuck the middle strand under one strand of the standing part, against the lay.
İkinci ve üçüncü kolu sok: Tuck the second and third strands
İkinci kolu bir sonraki kolun altından s: Tuck the second strand under the next strand; turn the rope over and tuck the third strand under the remaining strand. Each strand must come out at a different place.
Her kolu birinin üzerinden, diğerinin al: Continue tucking each strand over one and under one; make at least five rounds of tucks in synthetic rope, then trim the ends.
Üç kollu halatın ucunda kalıcı bir göz o: Forms a permanent eye in the end of a three-strand rope. It weakens the rope far less than a knot; the eyes of mooring lines are made this way.
Sentetik halat kaygan olduğundan doğal l: Synthetic rope is slippery and needs more tucks than natural fibre rope. If the first round of tucks is wrong the splice will twist, so check it carefully.
Halatın ucuna yakın uzun bir gözcük alın: Form a long bight near the end of the line.
Çımayı gözcüğün iki bacağının etrafına,: Wrap the working end tightly round both legs of the bight, working towards the end of the bight.
Çımayı gözden geçir: Pass the end through the eye
Yeterli sarımdan sonra çımayı gözcüğün u: After enough turns, pass the working end through the eye left at the end of the bight.
Bedeni çekip kilitle: Pull the standing part to lock
Bedeni çekerek gözü sarımların içine alı: Pull the standing part to draw the eye into the turns and trap the working end.
Atma halatının ucuna hızlıca ağırlık ver: A wrapped knot that quickly adds weight to the end of a heaving line. It is quicker to tie than a monkey's fist.
Sarımlar sık ve düzgün olmalıdır; gevşek: Keep the turns close and even; loose turns open up when the line is thrown.
Halatta bir kasa oluşturun ve kasayı bed: Make a loop in the line and lay it over the standing part.
Çubuğu kasanın bir kenarının üzerinden,: Pass the spike over one side of the loop, under the standing part and over the other side of the loop.
Halatı çekerek bağı çubuğa oturtun ve çu: Pull on the line to settle the hitch on the spike and use the spike as a handle.
Halata geçici olarak bir çubuk takar; çu: Attaches a spike or bar to a line temporarily, so that it can be used as a handle to haul lashings and seizings tight.
Çubuk çekilince bağ kendiliğinden çözülü: When the spike is withdrawn the hitch falls apart, so it holds only while the spike is in place.
Çımayı direğin etrafından veya ringin iç: Pass the working end round the post or through the ring.
Çımayla, kasanın içinde kalacak şekilde: Make two turns round the standing part inside the loop, the second turn jamming against the first.
Çımayla kasanın dışında bedenin etrafına: Finish with a half hitch round the standing part outside the loop.
Bağı beden boyunca kaydırarak gerginliği: Slide the hitch along the standing part to adjust the tension; under load it holds in place.
Halatın ucunda gerginliği ayarlanabilen: Forms an adjustable loop in the end of a line. It holds without slipping under load and, when the load is off, can be slid along the standing part to adjust the tension. Used for awning and lashing lines.
Kaygan halatta kasa içine bir volta daha: In slippery line, add one more turn inside the loop.
Bedende kasa oluştur: Make a loop in the standing part
Halatın bir ucunu bağlayın ve beden hala: Make one end fast and form a small loop in the middle of the standing part.
Çımayı alttaki bağlama noktasının (ring,: Pass the working end round the lower securing point (ring or hook).
Kasadan geçirip gerdir: Through the loop and haul taut
Çımayı kasanın içinden geçirin ve aşağı: Pass the working end through the loop and haul down on it to tension the line.
Gerginliği korurken çımayı iki yarım ane: Holding the tension, make the working end fast with two half hitches.
Halatı bir bağlama noktası üzerinden pal: Hauls a line taut over a securing point with the effect of a purchase and makes it fast. Used for lashing deck cargo, boats and covers.
Kasa olarak kayar bir kasa kullanılırsa: A slipped loop can capsize under heavy load; for heavy loads use a fixed loop instead.

1) Marka/model kullanıcı kitabını ve gem: 1) Check the make/model user manual and the ship's PMS plan. 2) Inspect the housing, antenna, bracket/HRU, battery expiry date and the 15 HEX ID registration. 3) Apply the manufacturer's SELF-TEST button and sequence; interpret the LED/beep or code result. The SELF-TEST may make a short, specially coded 406 MHz test transmission; saying 'there is no RF transmission at all' is wrong. 4) The GNSS self-test may be separate; follow the manufacturer's limit. 5) Position the beacon correctly in its bracket, verify that it is not sending an active distress alert and keep the GMDSS/PMS record. Do not use the normal ON/DISTRESS mode for routine testing: even a single transmission can trigger a SAR alert. 6) In a false alert, confirm that there is no real distress, switch it OFF and immediately inform the nearest RCC/MRCC of the HEX ID, position and time. 7) In a drill, show the position of the beacon, safe carrying and activation precautions without making a real distress transmission. Set the routine test frequency and button sequence according to the manufacturer; do not write a universal mandatory monthly procedure for all EPIRBs.

Lack of a GNSS fix does not always mean that the 406 MHz alert has stopped; satellite position solution techniques can be used. The 121.5 MHz signal is used for homing by nearby search and rescue craft and has not been monitored as a satellite alert since 2009. Modern AIS-EPIRBs can transmit a local AIS target position on AIS 1 (161.975 MHz) and AIS 2 (162.025 MHz); not every older beacon has AIS. Do not confuse the beacon's 15 HEX ID with the MMSI.
406–406.1 MHz, Cospas-Sarsat tehlike ika: 406–406.1 MHz is the digital transmission band used for Cospas-Sarsat distress alerting. The message contains the beacon's unique HEX identity and, if a GNSS position solution is available, the coordinates. The 121.5 MHz transmission helps suitably equipped search and rescue craft with final-stage direction finding (homing).

Açıkta normal ON/DISTRESS modunu rutin t: Do not use the normal ON/DISTRESS mode at sea for routine testing. If an operational test with a live transmission is required, it must be coordinated in advance with, and approved by, the competent RCC/authority.
AIS-EPIRB ve AIS-SART, uygun AIS alıcısı: AIS-EPIRBs and AIS-SARTs can be tracked with a SAR position symbol on a suitable AIS receiver/ECDIS display. The target may also appear on a radar display with AIS overlay switched on; however, this is not a 9 GHz radar response. It is not guaranteed that every AIS-EPIRB will appear on every radar.
AIS-EPIRB, AIS-SART ve radar-SART görünü: Distinguish between the AIS-EPIRB, AIS-SART and radar-SART displays.
Arızalı cihazın emniyet açısından uygunl: Escalate the safety suitability of the defective beacon according to the SMS.
Basınçla açılan HRU, su sensörü ve batar: The pressure-operated HRU, the water sensor and the battery are three separate elements. The HRU releases the beacon; the sensor triggers the electronics.
Batarya SKT/model ve son servis: Battery expiry date/model and last service
Batarya, HRU, shore-based maintenance ta: Manage the battery, HRU and shore-based maintenance dates according to the model/label/flag.
Bayrak, gemi adı, sahiplik, irtibat tele: The EPIRB registration must be updated when the flag, ship's name, ownership, contact telephone numbers or the beacon change. Wrong registration can lengthen SAR's verification time. Compare the registration details with the beacon label and the current official certificate.
Braketin serbest bırakma yönünü engellem: Do not obstruct the release direction of the bracket; do not tie the lanyard to the ship.
Cihazın üretici/model el kitabı ve PMS s: The beacon manufacturer's/model manual and the PMS interval are the basis. 1) Inspect the EPIRB for visible damage, its position in the bracket, the antenna, lanyard, HEX ID, and battery and HRU dates. 2) Apply the manufacturer-defined SELF-TEST button/sequence. 3) Assess the LED/beep/display result as PASS or FAIL; compare any error code with the manual. 4) If there is a separate GNSS self-test, carry it out only at the recommended interval and in accordance with the battery consumption warnings. 5) Place the beacon correctly in the bracket, verify that it is not transmitting; enter the date, time and test result in the GMDSS/PMS records.
Dahili GNSS alıcısı (GPS/Galileo vb.) fi: When the internal GNSS receiver (GPS/Galileo, etc.) obtains a fix, the EPIRB inserts the coordinates in the 406 MHz message, providing data in addition to the satellite position solution. Without a GNSS fix, the 406 MHz identity alert can continue, and the SAR network tries to determine the position by Doppler/MEOSAR processing. Loss of GNSS does not mean that the beacon has completely failed.

EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indicating Rad: The EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon) is a radio beacon with its own battery that sends a search and rescue alert via Cospas-Sarsat in grave and imminent danger. The 406–406.1 MHz digital distress message carries the 15-character HEX identity and, if available, the GNSS position. The chain satellite → LUT (Local User Terminal) → MCC (Mission Control Centre) → RCC/MRCC → SAR craft operates. 121.5 MHz is for local homing/direction finding by suitable SAR craft; since 2009 Cospas-Sarsat satellites have not processed 121.5 MHz distress alerts.

The EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon) is a position-indicating beacon with its own battery that sends a 406 MHz satellite distress message in grave and imminent danger such as abandoning ship or sinking. To use it technically correctly, the 406 MHz alert, 121.5 MHz homing, the new-generation AIS position transmission, the HRU/water sensor distinction, the test procedure and the radar-SART display must be kept apart. This training aims to enable the officer to check the beacon on board.
EPIRB → Cospas-Sarsat uydu faydalı yükü: EPIRB → Cospas-Sarsat satellite payload (LEOSAR, GEOSAR, MEOSAR) → ground terminal LUT (Local User Terminal) → MCC (Mission Control Centre) → the relevant RCC/MRCC (Rescue Coordination Centre) → search and rescue units. 'The signal goes to the satellite' describes only the first step of this chain.
EPIRB ile karşı tarafa sesli yanıt gönde: You cannot send a voice reply with an EPIRB; the RCC receiving the alert does not mean that every ship at sea detects you directly. With an AIS-EPIRB, local visibility depends on range and the AIS receiver/overlay status.
EPIRB kayıt bilgisi, onaylı bakım belges: The EPIRB registration details, approved maintenance document, last self-test, battery and HRU expiry dates and the HEX ID on the beacon label must match the records on board.
EPIRB onaylı float-free braketinde dış g: The EPIRB is stowed on the open deck in its approved float-free bracket. As the ship sinks, the hydrostatic pressure opens the Hydrostatic Release Unit (HRU) mechanism at about 1–4 m depending on the model. The beacon is released mechanically and floats to the surface; when the water sensor/electrodes get wet, the electronic circuit starts the transmission.
EPIRB radarda 12 nokta üretmez; radar-SA: An EPIRB does not produce 12 dots on radar; a radar-SART does, and an AIS-EPIRB may appear on the AIS display.
EPIRB self-test yapmak isterken yanlışlı: While trying to carry out an EPIRB self-test, ON/DISTRESS was activated by mistake. What should be done?
EPIRB, 406 MHz sayısal imdat alarmını Co: The EPIRB delivers a 406 MHz digital distress alert via Cospas-Sarsat to the RCC/MRCC. The operating frequencies and display presentations of the radar-SART, AIS-SART and AIS-EPIRB are different. This section teaches how the approved beacon is operated, tested and how its maintenance is tracked in real shipboard conditions.
EPIRB, çalışır durumdaki DSC, sesli MAYD: The EPIRB is not considered the only means of communication replacing a working DSC, voice MAYDAY and other GMDSS methods. In real distress, complementary distress means are used according to the ship's SMS and the Master's orders.
EPIRB, gemi radarına doğrudan hedef çize: An EPIRB is not a device that draws a target directly on the ship's radar; its primary function is to deliver a satellite distress alert to the SAR authority.
EPIRB'nin 121.5 MHz yayını ile 406 MHz y: What is the basic difference between an EPIRB's 121.5 MHz transmission and its 406 MHz transmission?
EPIRB'nin buoyant lanyard'ı gemiye ya da: The EPIRB's buoyant lanyard is not tied to the ship or to the float-free bracket; when necessary it can be attached to a survival craft or a person.
Float-free braketin HRU (Hydrostatic Rel: The HRU (Hydrostatic Release Unit) mechanism of the float-free bracket releases the beacon by pressure as the ship sinks, at about 1–4 m (depending on the model). The water sensor of the beacon that floats to the surface switches on the electronic circuit. The battery is not activated by seawater and does not generate energy from it: a sealed battery is already fitted. The front of the bracket must not be obstructed and the lanyard must not be tied to the ship; manual ON/DISTRESS is used according to the model manual when necessary.
Float-free EPIRB, serbest yüzmesine enge: A float-free EPIRB sits in an approved bracket so that nothing obstructs it from floating free. As the ship sinks, the HRU releases the beacon mechanically by hydrostatic pressure at a depth of about 1–4 m; the beacon floats to the surface and the water sensor activates the electronics. Seawater does not charge the battery or generate power; the beacon's pre-installed battery supplies the energy. Do not tie the lanyard to the ship or the bracket. IMO MSC.471(101) covers the relevant installations from 1 July 2022; it defines requirements such as a battery capacity of at least 48 hours, GNSS, 121.5 MHz and AIS locating. The standards for earlier installations may differ. Check the battery and HRU expiry dates on the actual label; do not apply a fixed 2/5 years to all models. Annual test: MSC.1/Circ.1040/Rev.2. Approved shore-based maintenance at intervals set by the flag and not exceeding 5 years: MSC.1/Circ.1039/Rev.1. Compare the current EPIRB 15 HEX ID registration with the flag/authority records.

Gerçek distress mevcutken alarmı sırf ya: If a real distress exists, do not switch off the alert just because it was activated by mistake; the decision about the transmission is made according to the real safety situation.
Gerçek distress testi yapma: Do not carry out a real distress test
Gerçek tehlike olmadığı doğrulanırsa der: If it is confirmed that there is no real distress, immediately switch the beacon OFF and inform the nearest RCC/MRCC by a suitable fast means. Report the beacon HEX ID, position, time of activation and false alert details. Just switching it off is not enough; the satellite alert may already have entered the SAR system.
Gerçek tehlike olmadığını doğrula ve yay: Confirm that there is no real distress and switch off the transmission immediately.
Gerçek tehlikede manuel aktivasyon üreti: In real distress, manual activation is carried out with the manufacturer's two-step safe sequence. On the sea surface the antenna must stay upright with a clear view of the sky. In the liferaft/lifeboat, check the beacon's indicator/light; do not keep the antenna under metal and do not tie the beacon to the sinking ship.
GNSS self-test bazı cihazlarda ayrı ve p: On some beacons the GNSS self-test is a separate test that consumes battery power.
HEX ID, mevki ve zamanı belirterek en ya: Report the false alert to the nearest RCC/MRCC, stating the HEX ID, position and time.
Hidrostatik basınç HRU'yu açar; su sensö: Hydrostatic pressure opens the HRU; the water sensor activates the beacon. The battery is already in place in the sealed beacon.
HRU bataryayı deniz suyuyla doldurur: The HRU fills the battery with seawater
HRU cihazı serbest bırakır; su sensörü ç: The HRU releases the beacon; the water sensor activates it; the battery is already fitted.
HRU doğrudan MRCC'ye sesli MAYDAY yollar: The HRU sends a voice MAYDAY directly to the MRCC
HRU mekanik serbest bırakır; su sensörü: The HRU releases mechanically; the water sensor activates; the battery does not start working with water.
The HRU releases mechanically; the water sensor triggers electronic activation
HRU mekanik serbest bırakma, su sensörü: The HRU provides mechanical release, the water sensor electronic activation.

HRU/kapak üstünde nesne, halat veya yapı: There must be no object, rope or adhesion on the HRU/cover; the EPIRB must be able to float to the surface unobstructed.
IMO MSC.1/Circ.1039/Rev.1 kapsamında yet: Under IMO MSC.1/Circ.1039/Rev.1, authorised shore-based maintenance is carried out at intervals set by the flag Administration and not exceeding 5 years. The HRU should not be fixed as 'always two years' or the EPIRB battery as 'always five years': the actual label, the approved product and the manufacturer's instructions are the basis.
IMO MSC.1/Circ.1040/Rev.2'nin yıllık tes: The annual test guidance of IMO MSC.1/Circ.1040/Rev.2 covers the physical condition, verification of registration, battery/HRU expiry dates, the 406 MHz self-test and, where possible, verification of the 121.5 MHz and AIS outputs, and bracket and label checks. A routine self-test in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions on board is not the same as the annual survey/test.
IMO MSC.471(101) kapsamında yeni standar: Under IMO MSC.471(101), the battery of an EPIRB subject to the new standard has an operating capacity of at least 48 hours. For real endurance, the battery expiry date, the beacon model and the service conditions are checked. Only the manufacturer's SELF-TEST function is used for testing: visual/label/HRU/expiry check → special TEST mode → check of the LED/error code → correct placement → GMDSS/PMS record. The self-test may make a short, specially coded RF test transmission but must not be a normal distress alert. Switching on ON/DISTRESS for a routine test can create a false SAR alert. On some models the GNSS self-test is separate and can drain the battery; the manufacturer's interval must be followed.
IMO MSC.471(101), ilgili EPIRB'nin batar: IMO MSC.471(101) requires the battery of the relevant EPIRB to have sufficient capacity to operate the beacon for at least 48 hours. This is a minimum performance requirement for the approved type. It cannot be read as a guarantee for a battery that is expired, damaged or unsuitable; the manufacturer's model label and flag requirements are taken into account.
İlgili standart −20°C ile +55°C işletim: The relevant standard includes requirements such as an operating temperature range of −20°C to +55°C, floating upright in water, a locating light visible at night and automatic float-free release before reaching a depth of 4 m.
Kendi geminin EPIRB modelindeki TEST pro: Apply the TEST procedure for your own ship's EPIRB model correctly.
Klasik 406 MHz EPIRB radarın X-band/S-ba: A conventional 406 MHz EPIRB does not create 12 dots on the X-band/S-band radar display. This characteristic presentation belongs to the radar-SART, which responds to 9 GHz X-band radar interrogation; 12 dots may be seen at a distance and arcs at close range. S-band radar does not trigger this response. An AIS-SART shows a special search and rescue target on a suitable AIS/ECDIS. An EPIRB with AIS can also make a local AIS position transmission; its appearing on the radar display with AIS overlay does not mean it is a real radar-SART response. Reception/antenna height, coverage and model requirements differ for each device. Do not teach a range advantage as a universal certainty.
Klasik 406 MHz EPIRB, ne X-band ne S-ban: A conventional 406 MHz EPIRB produces '12 dots' on neither X-band nor S-band radar. A radar-SART, on the other hand, responds to 9 GHz X-band radar pulses; typically 12 successive dots are seen on the radar display, and at close range the image may turn into arcs. S-band radar does not trigger a radar-SART in this way.
Logbook/PMS kaydını tamamlayıp tekrar ak: Complete the logbook/PMS entry and check whether reactivation/service is required.
Master gemiyi terk emri veriyor. Mümkün: The Master gives the order to abandon ship. As far as possible and safe, carry out distress communications by DSC and voice MAYDAY. The assigned person operates the EPIRB according to the manufacturer's instructions or makes sure the automatic float-free arrangement works unobstructed. The beacon's antenna stays facing the open sky; check the active indicator in the liferaft/lifeboat. Do not tie the EPIRB to the sinking ship.
MSC.471(101) kapsamında aktivasyondan so: Under MSC.471(101), after activation the GNSS position must be updated at intervals of not more than five minutes. However, because of satellite geometry, the antenna's view of the sky and processing conditions, an exact and immediate position is not guaranteed for every alert.
MSC.471(101) standardına tabi cihazın ya: On a beacon subject to the MSC.471(101) standard, merely removing it from the bracket by hand must not start a distress alert automatically. An older model may work differently: always follow the beacon's manual.
Onaylı self-test modunda özel formatlı k: In the approved self-test mode there may be a short, specially formatted RF test transmission; the statement 'it sends no RF signal at all' would be technically wrong. The test message is not processed by the satellite system as a real distress alert. However, switching the normal ON/DISTRESS mode on and off is not a routine check; even a single live transmission can lead to a SAR alert.
Pil deniz suyuyla güç üreten veya suyla: The battery is not a battery that generates power from seawater or is charged by water. The electrical energy comes from the pre-installed primary battery in the sealed housing; the water sensor only has a triggering function. Some brackets have a magnet/reed switch combination that detects the beacon being put back, and incorrect mounting can cause a false activation.
Radar ekranında 12 nokta dizisi hangi ci: A series of 12 dots on the radar display is the characteristic sign of which device?
Radar-SART'ın X-band nokta dizisini, AIS: Distinguish the X-band dot series of a radar-SART from the AIS target symbol of an AIS-EPIRB.
Rutin self-test = üretici test modu, ger: Routine self-test = the manufacturer's test mode, not the real distress ON.
Sadece cihazı kapatmak yeterli değildir;: Just switching off the beacon is not enough; the SAR coordinating authority must be informed.
Soru 1: EPIRB'nin pili suyla mı aktive o: Question 1: Is the EPIRB battery activated by water? Answer: No; the HRU releases the beacon, the water sensor switches on the electronics and the sealed battery is already fitted.
Soru 2: EPIRB 12 radar noktası oluşturur: Question 2: Does an EPIRB create 12 radar dots? Answer: No; a radar-SART does. An EPIRB with AIS gives its position on the AIS display.
Soru 3: Cihazın SELF-TEST yerine ON/DIST: Question 3: Is it acceptable to press ON/DISTRESS instead of the beacon's SELF-TEST and switch it off immediately? Answer: No; a real distress message may reach the SAR system. The self-test in the manual must be used.

EPIRB — THE DISTRESS ALERT CHAIN An Emer: EPIRB — THE DISTRESS ALERT CHAIN An Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon (EPIRB) broadcasts a digital distress signal in the 406–406.1 MHz band. The beacon transmits its unique 15-character HEX ID and, where available, GNSS position. Cospas-Sarsat satellites (LEOSAR, GEOSAR, MEOSAR) relay the alert to a Local User Terminal (LUT), Mission Control Centre (MCC), then the appropriate RCC/MRCC, which coordinates SAR resources. EPIRB is not a two-way VHF voice radio or an automatic marine radar target.

FLOAT-FREE ACTIVATION AND THE BATTERY A: FLOAT-FREE ACTIVATION AND THE BATTERY A float-free EPIRB is mounted in an unobstructed, approved cradle. As the vessel submerges, the Hydrostatic Release Unit (HRU) mechanically opens at approximately 1–4 m depth, depending on the model. The buoyant beacon rises and the water sensor activates its electronics. Seawater does NOT charge or power the battery; a pre-installed sealed battery provides the electrical energy. The beacon can also be activated manually according to its model's instructions. Never tie the buoyant lanyard to the sinking ship. Check for incorrect bracket/magnet/reed-switch placement after service.
